events.source_text: He had been hugged by a complete stranger.
Dumbledore hugged Mr. Dursley around the middle.
‘Er — Petunia, dear — you haven’t heard from your sister lately, have you?’
‘Funny stuff on the news,’ Mr. Dursley mumbled.
Albus Dumbledore didn’t seem to realize that he had just arrived in a street where everything from his name to his boots was unwelcome.
‘I’ve come to bring Harry to his aunt and uncle. They’re the only family he has left now.’
A huge motorcycle fell out of the air and landed on the road in front of them.
Dumbledore took Harry in his arms and turned toward the Dursleys’ house.
Hagrid swung himself onto the motorcycle and kicked the engine into life.
Dumbledore turned and walked back down the street.
He had a funny feeling he'd had the same dream before.
Up! Get up! Now!
Dudley punched Harry on the nose.
Aunt Petunia handed Dudley a large chocolate ice cream.
Harry looked intently at the snake.
Aunt Petunia flung her arms around Dudley.
The boa constrictor slithered out of its tank and snapped at Dudley's heels.
Harry sat up and gasped as the glass front of the boa constrictor's tank vanished.
By the time he was allowed out of his cupboard again
Dudley tried to grab the letter to read it
Aunt Petunia shredded the letters in her food processor
Uncle Vernon threw Harry into the hall
Uncle Vernon pointed at what looked like a large rock way out at sea
They reached the rock, where Uncle Vernon, slipping and sliding, led the way to the broken-down house
Aunt Petunia made up a bed for Dudley on the moth-eaten sofa
Uncle Vernon was in a very good mood
A toothless old man came ambling up to them, pointing, with a rather wicked grin, at an old rowboat bobbing in the iron-gray water below them
The storm raged more and more ferociously as the night went on
Harry heard something creak outside
The whole shack shivered and Harry sat bolt upright, staring at the door
Someone was outside, knocking to come in
They knocked again. Dudley jerked awake.
A giant of a man was standing in the doorway.
He strode over to the sofa where Dudley sat frozen with fear.
He bent down, picked up the door, and fitted it easily back into its frame.
‘Couldn’t make us a cup o’ tea, could yeh? It’s not been an easy journey…’
‘Las’ time I saw you, you was only a baby…’
‘Ah, shut up, Dursley, yeh great prune…’
‘Anyway — Harry, a very happy birthday to yeh. Got summat fer yeh here…’
Harry stretched out his hand at last to take the yellowish envelope…
He pulled out the letter and read…
‘Gallopin’ Gorgons, that reminds me…’
‘Given Harry his letter. Taking him to buy his things tomorrow…’
He rolled up the note, gave it to the owl…
‘He’s not going…’
‘I’m warning you, Dursley…’
‘If he wants ter go, a great Muggle like you won’t stop him…’
‘NEVER — INSULT-ALBUS-DUMBLEDORE-IN-FRONT-OF-ME!’
‘one more word…’
‘You’re a wizard, Harry…’
‘You’ll be famous…’

events.source_text: They walked down the road, and Hagrid tapped Harry on the shoulder.
‘We’re going to get yer school things, Harry. We’re going to get yer wand, and yer robes, and all the rest of it.’
They walked into Madam Malkin’s shop.
‘Hello,’ said the boy, ‘Hogwarts, too?’
Harry hopped down from the footstool.
They walked into Gringotts.
‘We’ve come ter take some money outta Mr. Harry Potter’s safe.’
They walked out of Gringotts.
They walked into Gringotts Vault 713.
Inside were mounds of gold coins.
They walked out of Gringotts Vault 713.
They walked into Madam Malkin’s shop.
‘Hello,’ said Harry. ‘My father’s next door buying my books and mother’s up the street looking at wands.’
Harry hopped down from the footstool.
They walked down the road.

‘You don’t have to —’ ‘Tell yeh what, I’ll get yer animal. Not a toad, toads went outta fashion years ago, yeh’d be laughed at — an’ I don’ like cats, they make me sneeze. I’ll get yer an owl. All the kids want owls, they’re dead useful, carry yer mail an’ everythin’.’
They walked down the road.
They walked into Flourish and Blotts.
They walked down the road.
They walked down the road.
They walked into Ollivanders.
They walked down the road.

Dumbledore reached out and patted her on the shoulder.
‘It certainly seems so,’ said Dumbledore.
Mr. Dursley hummed as he picked out his most boring tie for work, and Mrs. Dursley gossiped away happily as she wrestled a screaming Dudley into his high chair.
A man appeared on the corner the cat had been watching, appeared so suddenly and silently you’d have thought he’d just popped out of the ground.
Dumbledore reached out and patted her on the shoulder.
‘It certainly seems so,’ said Dumbledore.
Dumbledore took Harry in his arms and turned toward the Dursleys’ house.
Hagrid swung himself onto the motorcycle and kicked the engine into life; with a roar it rose into the air and off into the night.
The twinkling light that usually shone from Dumbledore’s eyes seemed to have gone out.

events.source_text: Nearly ten years had passed since the Dursleys had woken up to find their nephew on the front step,
‘Up! Get up! Now!’ Harry woke with a start.
‘Up!’ she screeched.
She jerked her head in Harry’s direction.
A moment later, Dudley’s best friend, Piers Polkiss, walked in with his mother.
‘Dinky Duddydums, don’t cry, Mummy won’t let him spoil your special day!’ she cried, flinging her arms around him.
The glass front of the boa constrictor’s tank had vanished.
The great snake was uncoiling itself rapidly, slithering out onto the floor.

events.source_text: Uncle Vernon took both Harry and Dudley by the scruffs of their necks and threw them into the hall
Uncle Vernon was pointing at what looked like a large rock way out at sea
Uncle Vernon’s rations turned out to be a bag of chips each and four bananas
The storm raged more and more ferociously as the night went on
Harry heard something creak outside
They knocked again. Dudley jerked awake.
“Who’s there?” he shouted.
“Las’ time I saw you, you was only a baby,” said the giant.
“Anyway — Harry,” said the giant, “a very happy birthday to yeh. Got summat fer yeh here — I mighta sat on it at some point, but it’ll taste all right.”
Harry pulled out the letter and read:
“Gallopin’ Gorgons, that reminds me,” said Hagrid,
With his tongue between his teeth he scribbled a note that Harry could read upside down:
Then he came back and sat down as though this was as normal as talking on the telephone.
“You never told him? Never told him what was in the letter Dumbledore left fer him? I was there! I saw Dumbledore leave it, Dursley! An’ you’ve kept it from him all these years?”
“Harry — yet a wizard.”
HOGWARTS SCHOOL of WITCHCRAFT and WIZARDRY Headmaster: ALBUS DUMBLEDORE
“Good question, Harry. Disappeared. Vanished. Same night he tried ter kill you. Makes yeh even more famous.”
Hagrid seized his umbrella and whirled it over his head, “NEVER,” he thundered, “- INSULT-ALBUS- DUMBLEDORE-IN- FRONT-OF- ME!”

events.source_text: They stood outside Gringotts, the wizarding bank.
‘Morning,’ said Hagrid to a free goblin.
Hagrid handed the goblin a small, golden key.
They were in a small cart, hurtling through a maze of twisting passages.
They stopped at last beside a small door in the passage wall.
Hagrid picked it up and tucked it deep inside his coat.
One wild cart ride later they stood blinking in the sunlight outside Gringotts.
They walked down Diagon Alley, back through the Leaky Cauldron, now empty.
They stopped to buy parchment and quills.
The train pulled out of the station.
